metaDescription: Answers about starting a kingdom, army training, banking, combat, account access, and getting help in OpenThrone.
title: Player FAQ
intro: A practical companion for your first decisions in the kingdom, and a place to turn when you need help.

game.title: What kind of game is OpenThrone?
game.answer: OpenThrone is a browser-based, text strategy MMORPG inspired by DarkThrone. You manage a kingdom, invest in an army and economy, and interact with other commanders. It is an independent project and is not affiliated with the original DarkThrone.

race.title: What should I know before choosing a race?
race.answer: The four races are Elf, Human, Goblin, and Undead. Each has different bonuses, so compare their descriptions in How to Play before choosing. No race automatically wins a matchup: army composition and equipment also matter.

firstSteps.title: What should I look at before my first investment?
firstSteps.answer: Start with your kingdom overview and check your gold, citizens, and army. Read the training cost before assigning citizens to a role, then compare equipment and structure upgrades. Keep enough gold for the next action you want to take; buying one upgrade can delay another.

training.title: How are training and equipment different?
training.answer: Training assigns citizens to army or economic roles. Workers contribute to your economy, attack soldiers support raids, defense soldiers guard your kingdom, and spies gather intelligence. Equipment is a separate investment through the Armory. Review quantities and total costs before submitting either purchase.

bank.title: Why can I not deposit all my gold at once?
bank.answer: Bank deposits have limits. A single deposit is limited to 80% of the gold you currently have on hand, and your account also has a limit on the number of deposits. The Bank shows deposit information and transaction history. Check those before planning a sequence of purchases or deposits.

combat.title: What should I check before attacking?
combat.answer: Review the target, your offensive strength, and the attack turns you plan to commit. Spy information can help you assess a target, but combat carries a risk of losses. After the battle, inspect the report and War History to understand the result before committing more resources.

protection.title: What does new-player protection cover?
protection.answer: A gold shield, not immunity. Attacks still take units and fort HP. Only your first {{allowance}} gold on hand is shielded — raiders take at most {{share}}% of the normal cap from it at level 1, rising to 100% at level {{taperLevel}}. Bank what you cannot defend; protected players can attack each other.

access.title: Why might I be unable to sign in?
access.answer: Read the message shown on the login page. Access may be restricted while login is disabled; a registered account does not guarantee that play is currently available. Check the public news for announcements. If the message does not explain your problem, ask for help without sharing your password or sign-in codes.

password.title: How do I recover a forgotten password?
password.answer: Request a reset on the password-reset page, then open the link in the email: it opens the page ready for you to choose a new password. The link works once and expires after 3 hours. Check your spam folder if the message does not arrive. Never post a reset link, password, or two-factor code in a public channel. If recovery still fails, describe the problem to support without including those secrets.

data.title: How do I get a copy of my data or delete my account?
data.answer: In Settings, under Your data, you can download a copy of your data and ask for your account to be erased. Both ask for your password first. An erasure is confirmed by email, then waits 14 days so you can change your mind. The same options are open to every player, wherever you live.

report.title: What information helps when reporting a bug?
report.answer: Include the page you were using, the action you took, what you expected, and what happened instead. Add the approximate time and a screenshot if it helps, after removing private messages, email addresses, and other sensitive details. The community Discord and the repository issue tracker are the support channels listed by the project.

allianceEra.title: What happens to my alliance when a new era starts?
allianceEra.answer: Your alliance is kept but reserved. Its name, roster, ranks and artwork stay, while its treasury, loans, troop contracts and wars end with the old era and its features stay locked. You can leave at any time, even before the leader acts. Only the leader can reactivate it, once they have reached level 10 in the new era and pay 10,000,000 gold.

allianceHall.title: How do alliance upgrades work?
allianceHall.answer: Your alliance's Alliance Hall sets three limits: how many members it holds, how often each member may deposit per 24 hours and how much the treasury can be filled by deposits. A new alliance starts at Camp: 10 members, 2 deposits per member per 24 hours and a 5,000,000 gold treasury. The leader, or a rank given "Buy upgrades", buys the next level with treasury gold on the Upgrades tab, which shows each level's cost, how many members it needs and its limits. A full alliance keeps every member but takes no new ones until it upgrades. A new era returns the hall to Camp.

allianceDues.title: Do alliances charge a fee or dues?
allianceDues.answer: An alliance may charge a one-time join fee (up to 10,000,000 gold) and membership dues collected daily (up to 1,000,000), weekly (up to 5,000,000) or monthly (up to 20,000,000 gold per member). Both come from your gold on hand and go to the treasury. The fee and dues show on the alliance card, the alliance page and the invitation, and you confirm them before you join. Dues are taken at each period start, never for time before you joined; if you cannot pay in full you pay what you have and owe the rest, which is taken first next time or can be paid from the alliance's Overview or Bank tab. Nobody is removed for unpaid dues, and the leader pays none. The leader, or a rank given "Set join fee and dues", changes them on the Settings tab. A new era clears unpaid dues.
